summary: A brother did chalitzah, and then the widow turned out to be expecting a baby. If the baby lives, the chalitzah meant nothing; if not, the chalitzah counts.
stIntro: When a man who has a brother dies childless, his widow [yevama] and one of his brothers [yavam] may perform a ritual through which she is freed of her levirate bonds [ḥalitza]. It is then considered, with regard to forbidden relationships, as though they had been married and divorced. Therefore, he is forbidden to her relatives, and she to his. However, with regard to

chunks.en: Someone who does chalitzah with his yevamah,
chunks.st: one who performs ḥalitza with his yevama and then

chunks.en: and she turns out to be expecting a baby, and she gives birth,
chunks.st: she is found to have been pregnant at the time of the ḥalitza and she gave birth,

chunks.en: if the baby lives,
chunks.explain: Then the dead brother has a child, so there was no yibum at all.
chunks.st: in the event that the offspring is viable, the deceased husband has been survived by offspring and so there was never any levirate bond; consequently, the ḥalitza that was performed was entirely unnecessary and a meaningless act. As such,

chunks.en: he is allowed to her relatives,
chunks.st: he remains permitted to her relatives

chunks.en: and she is allowed to his relatives,
chunks.st: and she remains permitted to his relatives.
chunks.stMore: Furthermore, since the ḥalitza was meaningless, she is not afforded the status of a ḥalutza, i.e., a yevama who performed ḥalitza, a status akin to that of a divorcée. Therefore, the ḥalitza

chunks.en: and it did not make her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: does not disqualify her from marrying into the priesthood.

chunks.en: If the baby does not live,
chunks.st: If the offspring is not viable, then it emerges that the ḥalitza was indeed necessary. Therefore,

chunks.en: he is forbidden to her relatives,
chunks.st: he is forbidden to engage in relations with her relatives

chunks.en: and she is forbidden to his relatives,
chunks.st: and she is forbidden to engage in relations with his relatives, as though they had been married and divorced,

chunks.en: and it made her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: and the ḥalitza disqualifies her from marrying into the priesthood, as she is afforded the status of a ḥalutza.

summary: A brother did yibum, and then the widow turned out to be expecting her first husband's baby. If the baby lives, the yibum was a mistake and they must separate. If it is not clear whose baby it is, they also separate.

chunks.en: Someone who marries his yevamah,
chunks.st: With regard to one who consummates the levirate marriage with his yevama, i.e., he had intercourse with her under the assumption that there is a levirate bond and so there is a mitzva to do so, and then

chunks.en: and she turns out to be expecting a baby, and she gives birth,
chunks.st: she is found to have been pregnant at the time of the intercourse and she gave birth,

chunks.en: if the baby lives,
chunks.st: in the event that the offspring is viable the deceased brother has been survived by offspring and it is evident that there was never any levirate bond.
chunks.stMore: In that case, the relations they had, rather than being a mitzva, were a violation of the prohibition against engaging in relations with one’s brother’s wife.

chunks.en: he must send her away, and they must bring a korban.
chunks.st: Therefore, the yavam must send her out, i.e., they must separate, as she is forbidden to him as his brother’s wife, and to atone for the forbidden relations that they had, they are each obligated to bring a sin-offering, as is the halakha for all who inadvertently transgress a prohibition that, when performed intentionally, is punishable by karet.

words.note: An animal brought to the Beis HaMikdash, here to make up for a sin.

chunks.en: And if the baby does not live,
chunks.st: And if the offspring is not viable, and therefore there was in fact a levirate bond,

chunks.en: he may keep her. If we are not sure if the baby is a nine-month baby from the first husband
chunks.st: he may maintain her as his wife since his intercourse with her was a valid consummation of levirate marriage. If they consummated the levirate marriage and seven months later she gave birth, there is uncertainty whether the child is nine months old, i.e., counting from conception, and is the offspring of the first husband, and as such there was no levirate bond, or

chunks.en: or a seven-month baby from the second,
chunks.st: whether the child is only seven months old and is the offspring of the latter husband, i.e., the yavam, and not of the deceased, in which case there was a levirate bond.

chunks.en: he must send her away, but the child is kosher,
chunks.st: In that case, due to the possibility that she is forbidden to him as his brother’s wife, he must send her out. However, the lineage of the child is unflawed, since regardless of whether it was born of the first or second husband, there was no transgression involved in its conception.

chunks.en: and they must bring an asham taluy.
chunks.st: Furthermore, to atone for the possibility that they had forbidden relations they are both obligated to bring a guilt-offering for uncertainty, as is the halakha for anyone who is uncertain whether they inadvertently transgressed a prohibition that would require one to bring a sin-offering.

words.note: A korban brought when someone is not sure if he sinned.

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁחַיָּבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם.
chunks.en: any one for whom the punishment is kareis from Heaven.
chunks.st: any forbidden relation for which one is liable to receive karet at the hand of Heaven.

chunks.en: And the halachah follows his words.
chunks.st: And the halakha is in accordance with his statement.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says: It is the offspring of a union with

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁחַיָּבִים עָלָיו מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין.
chunks.en: any one for whom beis din gives the death penalty.
chunks.st: any forbidden relation for which one is liable to receive court-imposed capital punishment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said:

chunks.he: מָצָאתִי מְגִלַּת יֻחֲסִין בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וְכָתוּב בָּהּ,
chunks.en: "I found a family-record scroll in Yerushalayim, and in it was written,
chunks.st: I found a scroll recording people’s lineages in Jerusalem, and it was written in it that

chunks.en: 'So-and-so is a mamzer from a married woman,'"
chunks.st: so-and-so is a mamzer from an adulterous union with a married woman, a sin punishable by court-imposed capital punishment.
chunks.stMore: The only reason for the scroll to state the reason that this individual is a mamzer is in order

chunks.en: which supports what Rabbi Yehoshua says.
chunks.st: to support the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua.
chunks.stMore: The mishna delineates the circumstances in which it is prohibited to engage in relations with the sister of one’s wife and the sister of one’s yevama:

chunks.en: If his wife died,
chunks.st: If a man’s wife died,

chunks.en: he is allowed to marry her sister.
chunks.st: he is permitted to her sister. If

chunks.en: If he divorced her and she died,
chunks.st: he divorced her and then

chunks.en: he is allowed to her sister.
chunks.st: she died, he is permitted to her sister. If he divorced his wife and then

chunks.en: If she married another man and died,
chunks.st: she was married to another and then

chunks.en: he is allowed to her sister.
chunks.st: died, he is permitted to her sister.

chunks.en: If his yevamah died,
chunks.st: If his yevama died,

chunks.en: he is allowed to her sister.
chunks.st: he is permitted to her sister. If

chunks.en: If he did chalitzah with her and she died,
chunks.st: he performed ḥalitza with her and then

chunks.en: he is allowed to her sister.
chunks.st: she died, he is permitted to her sister. If after ḥalitza she was married to another and then died, he is permitted to her sister.
chunks.stMore: The principle underlying all these cases is that the prohibition against engaging in relations with her sister only applies while the wife or yevama remain alive, irrespective of their current relationship to the man.
